Question: All of the even numbers from \(2\) to \(98\) inclusive, excluding those ending in \(0,\) are multiplied together. What is the rightmost digit (the units digit) of the product?
Solution:
Only the units digits of the factors affect the units digit of their product: every contribution involving a ten is a multiple of \(10\).

The included factors form ten groups:
\[
(2,4,6,8),\quad(12,14,16,18),\quad\ldots,\quad(92,94,96,98).
\]
These groups include every required factor exactly once. Each group has units digits \(2,4,6,8\), and
\[
2\cdot4\cdot6\cdot8=384,
\]
so each group product ends in \(4\).

Pair the ten groups to obtain five larger groups. Each larger group has a product ending in \(6\), because \(4\cdot4=16\). Multiplying two numbers ending in \(6\) again gives a number ending in \(6\), since \(6\cdot6=36\). Thus multiplying all five larger-group products leaves units digit \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
